newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Former Murdoch headquarters gutted by fire.
newsitem.headline: Former Murdoch headquarters gutted by fire.

text.p: The building where mogul Rupert Murdoch launched his global media empire 40 years ago was destroyed by fire Wednesday.

Murdoch began his career as a newspaper owner in the 1950s in the four-story building in this city in South Australia, which had been the headquarters of a stable of newspapers owned by his father, Sir Keith Murdoch.
Twenty fire engines and 50 firefighters were unable to stop the blaze, which spread to a nearby hotel.
"We have no cause and we have no estimates of damage at this stage," a fire department spokesman said.
The art deco-style grey stone building, built in 1924, was home to the The News, Rupert Murdoch's first newspaper, which closed in 1994.
The building had been vacant for some years.
Murdoch, now a U.S. citizen, heads the global media group News Corp., which has interests worldwide in films, television, publishing and newspapers.
